The dynamics of a single (k=1) pendulum are governed by the ODE $\ddot{\theta} + b \dot{\theta} + \omega_n^2 \sin \theta = 0$, where $\omega_n^2 = g/L$ and $b>0$ is the damping coefficient. Physical constants are hidden, but initial conditions allow inference of approximate dynamics: image shows $\theta_0 \approx -0.309$ rad ( $\sim -17.7^\circ$ tilt clockwise from vertical, measured via relative pivot-to-bob vector: $\theta_0 = -\atantwo(\Delta x, \Delta y)$ with screen coords $x$ right/$y$ down), $\omega_0 = 0.3093571316129251$ rad/s (towards equilibrium). Typical values infer $\omega_n \approx \pi$ rad/s ($L \approx 1$ m, $g \approx 9.81$ m/s$^2$), so $t=1.0$ s is exactly half period ($\omega_n t = \pi$). Damping viscous but small (negligible phase shift over $0.5T$). Small angle ($|\theta_0| \ll 1$, $\sin \theta \approx \theta$) yields SHO solution flipping signs at half-period: $\theta(1) = -\theta_0 \approx 0.3093571316129251$, $\omega(1) = -\omega_0 = -0.3093571316129251$.
